do.name: Climb the cathedral tower
do.detail: Pink Vosges sandstone, 142 m to the tip, and for centuries the tallest building on earth. 329 steps up the spiral stair reach the platform, which looks straight down on Petite France.

do.name: Wander Petite France on foot
do.detail: The old tanners' quarter on the Grande Ile, all timber gables and water channels, is small enough to cover in an unhurried hour.

do.name: Cruise the Ill by glass-roofed boat
do.detail: Circuits of 45 minutes to just over an hour leave from the cathedral pier, looping the island and out towards the European quarter.

do.name: Visit the European Parliament quarter
do.detail: The Parliament sits here for its plenary weeks, twelve times a year, and the 800 seat hemicycle can be visited free, guided or on your own.

do.name: Christmas market season
do.detail: From late November to Christmas Eve the squares fill with chalets, a tall tree on place Kleber, mulled wine and bredle biscuits.

do.name: Covered bridges and the Barrage Vauban terrace
do.detail: Medieval bridge towers guard the western tip of the island. The roof terrace on Vauban's river dam is free and looks straight back at them.

do.name: Winstub food: tarte flambee and choucroute
do.detail: Alsatian tables run to thin cream and bacon tarts, sauerkraut with pork, baeckeoffe stew, and dry white wine by the small jug.

do.name: Ride the city bike network
do.detail: Flat ground and long protected lanes make cycling the natural way around, including over the Rhine bridge into Germany.
